safety.notice: Educational identification only. This tool cannot reliably determine whether a snake is dangerous. Never approach, touch, capture, or handle a snake to obtain a photograph. If a snakebite has occurred, seek immediate medical care. Do not wait for an identification result.
safety.headline: If a snakebite has occurred, seek immediate medical care. Do not wait for online identification.
safety.call: Call 1990 for a free ambulance (Suwa Seriya)
safety.callNote: Or go straight to the nearest hospital. Number verified against 1990.lk on 11 October 2026.
do: Keep the person calm, still and lying down.
Keep the bitten limb still, as if it were broken. A splint or sling helps.
Remove rings, bangles, anklets and tight clothing near the bite before swelling starts.
Get to a hospital as quickly as possible, ideally one with a medical officer.
Note the time of the bite and any symptoms to tell the doctor.
dont: Don't tie a tourniquet or tight band.
Don't cut, burn or suck the wound.
Don't apply herbs, ice, chemicals or traditional pastes.
Don't try to catch or kill the snake, or spend time photographing it.
Don't wait to see whether symptoms develop.
safety.why: Hospitals treat snakebite based on symptoms and clinical tests. A photograph is not needed, and searching for one costs time.
safety.slma: Read the Sri Lanka Medical Association's snakebite guidance
safety.reviewed: Based on SLMA and WHO guidance. Content should be reviewed by a medical professional before any public deployment.

home.title: Every pattern has a story.
home.lede: Explore the remarkable diversity of Sri Lanka's snakes, their habitats, their behaviour, and their place in our natural world.
home.featuredText: A first selection of common, endemic and medically important species. Each profile lists its sources.
home.habitatText: From Sinharaja's canopy to the sandy north-west, each habitat has its own set of snakes.
home.moveText: No legs, four strategies. Choose one to watch it work.
home.mythText: Tap a card to see what the evidence says.
home.identifyText: Compare a photograph with our guide. You'll get possible matches to learn from, never a verdict on whether a snake is safe.
home.respectText: Most bites happen when people try to catch, kill or move a snake. Stay still, step back slowly and let it leave.
home.plateNote: Ambush hunter. Rests motionless on branches for hours.

library.title: Snake library
library.lede: A curated, growing field guide. It is not a complete list of Sri Lanka's snakes.
library.search: Search by English, Sinhala, Tamil or scientific name
library.empty: No species match those filters. Clear a filter or try another spelling.
library.compareHint: Select up to three species to compare.

profile.limitationsNote: No single feature guarantees an identification, or tells you whether it is safe to approach a snake.
profile.noFolklore: No documented folklore has been added for this species yet.
profile.notFound: We couldn't find that species. It may have been renamed.

compare.title: Compare species
compare.lede: Side by side, with the reasons appearance can mislead.
compare.empty: Choose two or three species to compare.
compare.warning: Appearance varies between individuals, ages, sexes, locations, lighting and camera angles. Use comparisons to learn, not to decide whether a snake is safe.

identify.title: Identify a snake
identify.lede: An experimental, non-diagnostic guide. Your photo stays on your device.
identify.drop: Choose a photo from your device
identify.dropHint: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 10 MB
identify.privacy: Your photo is processed only in this browser. It is never uploaded, and no location or metadata is read.
identify.errType: That file type isn't supported. Choose a JPEG, PNG or WebP image.
identify.errSize: That photo is larger than 10 MB. Choose a smaller image.
identify.errRead: This image couldn't be opened. Try another photo.
identify.noPhoto: No photo? You can still answer the questions.
identify.modelNote: No validated Sri Lankan snake-recognition model is available yet, so this guide does not use AI to name species. Instead, compare your photo with the questions below. Each answer narrows the list of possible matches.
identify.colourHint: Suggested from your photo's colours: {c}. Check it yourself.

a.ground: On the ground or leaf litter

identify.resultsLede: These species share the most features with your answers. The list may be wrong or incomplete.
identify.unclear: These answers don't narrow things down reliably. Several quite different species fit equally well, so we can't suggest a likely match. Browse the library or compare the species below.
identify.tooFew: Answer at least two questions to see possible matches.
identify.aiPrivacy: To suggest species, your photo is resized, stripped of location data and sent through our server to Google Gemini. This site doesn't store it; Google processes it under its API terms.
identify.aiNote: Suggestions come from Google Gemini, a general-purpose AI model. It has not been validated on Sri Lankan snakes and can be wrong. Use it to start learning, never to decide whether a snake is safe.
identify.aiNotSnake: The AI doesn't see a snake in this photo. Try a clearer photo, or answer the questions below.
identify.aiUnclear: The AI couldn't make out the animal clearly, so treat these suggestions with extra caution.
identify.aiPoor: Photo quality is poor, so these suggestions are especially uncertain.
identify.aiNone: The AI couldn't suggest a species from this photo. Answer the questions below instead.
identify.aiError: The AI service isn't available right now. You can still answer the questions below.
identify.aiQuota: The AI service has reached its usage limit for now. Try again later, or answer the questions below.
identify.refine: Refine by describing what you see
identify.ledeAi: An experimental, non-diagnostic guide. Your photo leaves your device only if you choose AI analysis.

habitats.title: Explore habitats
habitats.lede: Choose a habitat to see species documented there. Zones on the map are generalised and do not show exact locations.
habitats.mapAlt: Simplified map of Sri Lanka showing the wet zone in the south-west, the dry zone across the north and east, and the intermediate zone between them.

knowledge.title: Knowledge corner
knowledge.lede: Behaviour, movement, myths and the science of living alongside snakes.
knowledge.movementNote: Movement depends on the species, the surface and the situation. Not every snake uses every pattern, and movement is never an identification test.
knowledge.folkloreLede: Legends, traditions and beliefs about snakes from across Sri Lanka, with where each comes from. Folklore is culture, not zoology, and it's labelled that way.

sources.title: About and sources
sources.lede: Ceylon Serpents is an educational field guide. Every species profile lists the references it is based on.
sources.about: This project is a portfolio prototype built as a static website. It has no backend, account system or tracking. Content was compiled from the sources below and is labelled where translations or details are provisional.
sources.reviewText: Scientific names follow The Reptile Database. Local names are marked verified only where they match a Sri Lankan source. Safety text follows SLMA and WHO guidance. Before public launch, species text should be checked by a herpetologist, safety text by a medical professional, and Sinhala and Tamil text by native-speaking reviewers.
sources.creditNote: Photographs were supplied as references in the project brief. Their licences have not been verified. Replace them or obtain permission before publishing.
limits: The species list is a starting selection, not a complete checklist.
Some Sinhala and Tamil names and translations are missing or provisional.
AI photo suggestions come from a general-purpose model (Google Gemini) that has not been validated on Sri Lankan snakes.
Conservation assessments have not yet been added.

footer.note: An educational field guide to Sri Lanka's snakes. Not a medical or emergency service.
footer.made: Built as a static, privacy-respecting site. No tracking.
